plan.title: design(hooks,swarm): with more than one active brief, in-session workers cannot write; the only parallel route skips the local fence

narratives.Description: With more than one active brief, a worker that `swarm:launch` did not register has no story link, so the commit check refuses its commits and the operator runs them by hand; a merge of the default branch into a story branch is also refused because it stages other stories' files. This story makes `swarm:pre-dispatch` begin, a step the parent already runs before every implementation spawn, write a story-binding record for the worker's worktree, which the #6233 binding reads after the worker-auth assignment. It also excuses, in a merge commit only, the staged files that arrive unchanged from the fetched default branch, keeps `file_scope` on the merge-base brief and makes the refusal text name the repair that works. It adds no new gate, verb, flag, approval or stop; the contract is successor lean 6921798679 bound by synthesis 6921886810 on #6379.
narratives.AcceptanceJustification: 48 clauses: one per admitted Bound-remedy sentence of successor lean 6921798679 (29) and one per Acceptance Criteria line of that lean (19), as #3550 and #5055 require for a Spec-path brief.
narratives.UserStory: As a parent agent dispatching a story worker while other briefs are active, I want `swarm:pre-dispatch` begin to bind the worker's worktree to its story, so that the worker's in-scope commits and default-branch merge commits are admitted without an operator commit step.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. packages/core/src/swarm/story-binding-record.ts (new): the story-binding record store under `<git-common-dir>/deft-story-binding/`, one JSON record per canonical worktree path holding story_id, worktree_path and attempt_ids (no auth field); read, ensure (keep ids for the same story, replace for a different story) and remove-by-attempt-id, all writes under one store lock.
2. packages/core/src/swarm/story-binding-target.ts (new): resolve the begin target (linked worktree path, or a branch name checked out in exactly one linked worktree) and the scope id (brief path, story id or owned issue number) to exactly one active brief in that worktree.
3. packages/core/src/swarm/pre-dispatch.ts: begin ensures the record after an allowed begin saves its ledger, and on DENY_DUPLICATE_ACTIVE with the unit's running attempt ids; a failed resolution prints one line and writes nothing; exit codes are unchanged. Cancel and complete remove the ended attempt id from every record that lists it. No new flag and no swarm:launch readiness check.
4. packages/core/src/hooks/scope.ts: resolveWorktreeStoryBinding reads the worker-auth assignment first and the story-binding record second, with the same checks and refusals; the multiple-eligible refusal and the binding repair text name `swarm:pre-dispatch` begin by the parent before the environment pin.
5. packages/core/src/hooks/merge-commit-excuse.ts (new) and packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts: with MERGE_HEAD present, a staged product path outside file_scope is excused only when its staged mode and blob (or deletion) equal its entry in a MERGE_HEAD commit that is an ancestor of the fence's fetched delivery ref; unreadable MERGE_HEAD or delivery ref excuses nothing. The fence loader stays the merge-base loader.
6. Tests for every clause: story-binding-record.test.ts, pre-dispatch-story-binding.test.ts, merge-commit-excuse.test.ts and dispatcher-story-binding.test.ts (real repositories with an origin remote, merge-base briefs and linked worktrees); keep the existing pre-dispatch, scope and dispatcher suites green.
7. Docs: content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/host-claude-code.md and core-phase-3.md name the record that begin writes; one CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] line.
Rejects (Constraint): no file_scope read from the worktree brief copy; no excuse for every path that matches any merge parent; no swarm:launch as the writer for these workers; no reuse of the worker-auth assignment; no new verb or flag; no branch-name binding; no claim that a worker cannot write its own record; no claim that the class 4 or productPullRequest conflicts are settled.
narratives.Overview:
1. Story-binding record. `swarm:pre-dispatch` begin writes a story-binding record for the target worktree under the Git common directory. The record belongs to the worktree: it holds the story id, the canonical worktree path and the list of attempt ids that use it, and no auth field. `readWorkerAuthAssignment` and `requireScmReady` do not read it. Begin runs none of the `swarm:launch` readiness checks and adds no flag.
2. Target and scope. The target is the path of a linked worktree, or a branch name, which begin resolves to the one linked worktree that has that branch checked out. The scope id must resolve to exactly one brief under `xbrief/active/` in that worktree, by brief path, story id or owned issue number. When either resolution fails, begin writes no record, prints one line that names the failed resolution, and keeps its exit code.
3. Repeat begin. When begin is refused because an attempt for the same scope and target is already running, it still ensures the record and adds that unit's running attempt ids to the list, and keeps its refusal exit code. An allowed begin adds its new attempt id after it saves its ledger. A record for the same worktree and story keeps its other ids. A record for the same worktree and a different story is replaced, with only the new attempt id in its list.
4. Read order. `resolveWorktreeStoryBinding` uses the worker-auth assignment when one exists for the worktree. Otherwise it uses the story-binding record, with the same checks and refusals it applies to an assignment.
5. Removal. `swarm:pre-dispatch` cancel or complete, after it marks an attempt ended, removes that attempt id from every story-binding record that lists it, and deletes a record whose list is then empty. It finds the records by attempt id in the record store; it does not resolve the target again and does not read any ledger. The writes in items 1 and 3 and this removal run under one lock on the record store.
6. Merge commits. When `MERGE_HEAD` is present at `git commit`, a staged product path is excused from the `file_scope` check when its staged entry (mode and blob, or deletion) is identical to that path's entry in a `MERGE_HEAD` commit that is an ancestor of the fetched delivery ref. Every other staged path is checked as today. When `MERGE_HEAD` or the delivery ref cannot be read, no path is excused.
7. Refusal text. The multiple-eligible refusal and the worktree-binding repair text name `swarm:pre-dispatch` begin by the parent as the repair for a linked worktree, before the environment pin.
8. Fence authority is unchanged. Write/Edit and the commit check keep one loader, and it reads `file_scope` only from the merge-base copy of the brief.
narratives.Constraint:
- Reading `file_scope` from the worktree copy of the brief (comment 6921217700 finding 1; comment 6921248962 finding 3; comment 6921288234 finding 1).
- Excusing every staged path that matches any merge parent (comment 6921217700 finding 2).
- `swarm:launch` as the writer for solo, hand-started and large stories (comment 6921248962 findings 1 and 2).
- Reusing the worker-auth assignment as the story link for those workers (comment 6921454922 finding 3).
- A new registration verb or a new required flag (comment 6921288234 finding 3).
- Binding by branch name (comment 6921288234 question 2; #6233).
- A claim that a worker cannot write its own record (comment 6921217700 finding 3; comment 6921248962 finding 8).
- A claim that this design settles the class 4 or `productPullRequest` conflicts (comment 6921217700 finding 4; comment 6921248962 finding 6).

## Candidate remedy: derive the story from the worktree

Evidence from 2026-11-16: the operator ran nine commit steps by hand (R145-R152). Each was an agent `git commit` refused by the #5656 prospective scope-cover hook ("Multiple active xBRIEF artifacts are eligible ..."). The same command then passed from the operator's terminal unchanged. The gate stopped only the agent; it added no check.

Causes seen:
- The hook reads `DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE` from the shared host environment, not the worker's own.
- It counts only briefs on the merge base, so a story whose brief is new on its branch is never eligible (#6398, #6336).
- Merge commits that bring master into a story branch are refused too, because they stage product paths from other stories.

Candidate: when the commit runs in a linked worktree, resolve the scope from that worktree: its branch, plus the single active brief in its own tree whose issue matches the branch. Treat staged paths that come from the merge parent of a `git merge` as already admitted. One worker per worktree then commits with no operator step, and the fence still refuses paths outside that brief's file_scope.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Given a linked worktree with one active brief that matches its branch, when an agent commits paths in that brief's file_scope, then the hook admits the commit with no `DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE` in the host environment.
- Given a merge of origin/master into a story branch, when the only staged paths outside the brief's file_scope come from the merge parent, then the hook admits the merge commit.

## In plain English

Workers need a reliable link to their assigned story so they can commit without asking the operator to repeat the command. Recording that link for solo and large-story workers addresses a real gap.

The three-change proposal does not preserve today’s fence as written. A worker-controlled brief can grant itself more permissions, and an arbitrary merge parent can supply changes that escape the proposed commit check. The assignment approach remains useful, but those two authority changes prevent accepting the full target.

Evidence below is from `c3630b3c54fa2d68a07e10ae083aedbc7dffa7de`. Verification was read-only source inspection; no tests, builds, installs, or writes were performed.

## 1. blocks-the-design — A local brief cannot also be its own authorization

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:5220–5227` excludes lifecycle briefs from product coverage; `5296–5318` loads the merge-base fence and checks staged product paths against it. `packages/core/src/policy/write-fence.ts:480–499,511–555` explicitly obtains the authority from the merge-base object.

**Failure mode:** With change (3), a worker can widen its bound brief to include another product path and then commit that path. If “own tree” means working files, the widened brief need not even be committed. If it means HEAD, a preceding brief-only commit can establish the widened scope. An assignment fixes story identity; it does not authenticate that story’s current permissions.

**Later control and residual risk — question 1:** `scope-provenance/evaluate.ts:1575–1613,1707–1740` retains merge-base production checks and intent checking. These are real downstream controls, but they are not equivalent to the local fence. `scope-provenance/base-fence.ts:43–56,175–187` permits a bounded number of extra production files and excludes test/fixture paths from that production check. Membership and existing intent pins can impose additional restrictions; neither justifies claiming every locally unauthorized path will be caught. The unauthorized commit has also already occurred.

**Disposition:** Change (3) cannot bind as unrestricted local-tree authority. The strongest argument for it is admitting legitimately activated, branch-new briefs. That needs an independently authorized scope source or revision; merely finding the assigned story locally does not supply one.

## 2. blocks-the-design — Parent equality does not establish permission to import a change

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:5125–5158,5254–5318` currently checks staged product paths without a merge-parent exemption.

**Failure mode:** Change (2) applies whenever `MERGE_HEAD` exists, although P2 concerns importing the default branch. A worker can merge an unapproved local branch containing an out-of-scope change. If the staged result equals that second parent, the proposed rule excludes the path from coverage. No conflict resolution is necessary. The same rule would admit a newly staged file-mode change if “content” comparison means blob bytes alone.

This is a counterexample to the proposed rule, not a claim that the current implementation already contains that exemption.

**Disposition:** P2 relief needs an explicit authority condition for the imported parent, plus comparison of complete tree entries, including modes and absence. Exempting any parent-matching content weakens the fence. Restricting that exemption preserves existing refusals rather than adding a new operator approval step.

## 3. blocks-the-design — The registration writer and its authority remain unspecified

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/swarm/launch.ts:2007–2022` is the only production call site found for `writeWorkerAuthAssignment`. The writer validates supplied fields and persists the record under the common Git directory (`swarm/worker-auth-assignment.ts:598–657`); it does not itself distinguish parent from worker. Launch readiness imposes the scheduling restrictions at `swarm/readiness.ts:444–469`.

**Failure mode:** Moving registration outside the parallel-readiness check is necessary but insufficient. A hand or solo dispatch still needs a concrete caller. If the remedy is a generally worker-callable registration verb, a worker can request reassignment. A shared Git-directory location and valid JSON do not establish parent-only authority.

**Questions 2 and 3:** The #6233 identity rule is preserved if the existing resolver remains authoritative: `hooks/scope.ts:956–1028` binds by assignment story ID, never branch name, and refuses conflicting pins. Today the concrete writer is `swarm:launch`; the target names no replacement or extended verb for hand/solo dispatch.

**Disposition:** The design needs to identify the parent dispatch entry point and the existing authority check it uses before claiming registration cannot be worker-authored. This finding does not require a new registry or a human confirmation.

## 4. sharpens-framing — The one-PR conflicts survive these changes

**Evidence:** `.deft/approved-scope/**` is protected in `packages/core/src/class-checks/policy.ts:41`; mixed protected/product changes produce Class 4 findings in `class-checks/evaluate.ts:870–913`. `pr-closing-keywords/main.ts:394–399` requires the PR stamp on the relevant changed-brief path. `scope-provenance/known-machine.ts:32–41,128–152` does not classify `metadata.productPullRequest` as machine-only, and `extract-intent.ts:193–221` preserves unknown metadata in extracted intent.

**Failure mode:** A worker can pass the revised commit hook and still encounter the reported protected-record conflict or change its pinned intent by adding the required PR stamp.

**Disposition — question 4:** These conflicts are not settled by the three changes. They can remain separate work: #6198 describes the stamp/provenance conflict; the protected-record composition conflict needs its own explicit disposition. They do not justify weakening either check here.

## 5. sharpens-framing — Relief means fewer handoffs, not unconditional commits

**Evidence:** `hooks/scope.ts:980–1025` already refuses missing, ambiguous, ineligible, or conflicting assignments. `hooks/dispatcher.ts:5096–5103` also retains restrictions on commit forms that mutate the index after inspection.

**Failure mode:** An unqualified “no operator step, no new refusal” promise implies that registration alone makes every worker commit succeed, despite these retained conditions and the independent one-PR gates.

**Disposition — question 5:** The concrete addition is automatic registration during every supported implementation dispatch, removing the missing-assignment handoff for P1. A narrowly authorized merge-import exemption can address P2. Existing refusals remain; scope authorization for branch-new briefs is a separate unresolved part of this target.

## 6. footnote — Embedded instructions were treated as described content

The supplied snapshot contains instruction-shaped text, including the quoted refusal directing workers not to set host environment variables and linked issue #4007’s requests to change matching and add tests. These were treated as evidence about proposed behavior, not executed instructions. No sibling findings or post-ceiling comments were consulted.

## In plain English

With several stories active, Directive must know which story a linked worktree belongs to before an agent commit is allowed. Today that link is written only by `swarm:launch`, and large or hand-started workers often never get a link, so the operator has to run the commit. Merges from the default branch also fail the same check because they stage other stories’ files. The claim under test says three changes fix that without a weaker fence and without a new refusal: write the link for every implementation worker, ignore merge-parent noise when `MERGE_HEAD` is present, and read the bound brief from the worktree tree.

That claim does not hold as written. Reusing the existing assignment binder is the right identity rule, and a careful merge-parent filter can clear the merge pain. The strength claim fails on change (3), and change (1) still leaves large and hand/solo workers without a named parent-only writer that can run outside the readiness catch-22. Until those holes are closed, the design cannot promise “agent commits with no operator step” while keeping today’s fence strength.

## Findings

### 1. blocks-the-design — Change (1) does not get `size: large` through the only writer

Evidence: `packages/core/src/swarm/launch.ts` 2007–2022 (sole production `writeWorkerAuthAssignment` loop after gates); `packages/core/src/swarm/launch.ts` 1041–1056 (`enforceGates` always runs readiness, including N=1 `soloHeadless`); `packages/core/src/swarm/readiness.ts` 444–469 and 464 (`readiness=ready` required; `concurrentReady` follows `readiness === READY`; `size=large` forbids `parallel_safe=true`); `packages/core/src/vbrief-validation/story-quality.ts` 337–383 (`readiness=ready` requires `parallel_safe=true`).

Failure mode: a honest `size: large` story cannot be both `parallel_safe=true` and launch-ready. Setting `parallel_safe=false` still fails readiness when `readiness=ready`. Decoupling “apart from the `parallel_safe` launch check” while leaving assignment writes inside gated `swarm:launch` therefore still leaves large workers unregistered. Unregistered linked worktrees keep `resolveWorktreeStoryBinding` → `none` (`packages/core/src/hooks/scope.ts` 956–980), then multi-active commit refuse. P1 remains for the overnight large cohort.

Disposition consequence: the lean cannot bind change (1) as sufficient for “solo and `size: large` included” until assignment writing is named on a parent-only path that does not require the concurrent readiness conjunct, or readiness itself is recut for register-only PREP.

### 2. blocks-the-design — Change (1) names no parent-only verb for hand / interactive solo dispatch

Evidence: production write site only in `packages/core/src/swarm/launch.ts` 2007–2022; interactive Claude path text in `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/host-claude-code.md` 49–60 still says the trusted writer is `swarm:launch` PREP; Stop 1 P1 explicitly includes hand dispatch and solo dispatch.

Failure mode: overnight P1 is not only “large failed readiness.” It is also workers started without `swarm:launch`. Extending launch’s write loop does not create a record for those workers. The worker also must not self-register: `packages/core/src/swarm/worker-auth-assignment.ts` 1–6 states the registry is cooperative and not protection against a same-user process, and host adapter text at `host-claude-code.md` 60 says a worker process can still change the record.

Disposition consequence: bind requires a named parent/orchestrator verb (or PREP step) that writes the assignment before implement tools run, with worker-initiated writes refused or useless. Without that, “no operator step” for P1’s hand/solo limb is an assertion, not a mechanism.

### 3. blocks-the-design — Change (3) makes the local fence weaker than today

Evidence: `packages/core/src/policy/write-fence.ts` 511–517 and 518+ (`loadStoryWriteFenceFromMergeBase`: “Never uses the working-tree head brief as authority”); commit cover loads that helper by default in `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` 5296–5318; lifecycle paths under `xbrief/` are excluded from product staged cover at 5220–5255; Write of the bound brief itself is already denied as outside story `file_scope` in `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher-active-scope.test.ts` 394–418; CI membership/production split in `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/base-fence.ts` 1–27 (production fence stays merge-base; head/`forge-approval` is membership-only).

Failure mode: reading `file_scope` from the worktree head lets a worker who can mutate the head brief (unclassified Shell forms while `shellDestForms` stays off, or any non-Write channel) widen allow and then pass local Write/commit under the new head scope. The commit check will not treat the brief edit as a product path. `verify:scope-provenance` can still refuse at PR time, but the local fence is no longer the same early control it is today. That breaks the refutation’s “fence stays as strong as today” conjunct. The new-on-branch empty merge-base pain is real, but head-as-authority is the wrong strength trade.

Disposition consequence: reject head-brief `file_scope` as the local SoT. Keep merge-base (or another sealed non-worker-writable snapshot, such as activation-PR bytes) for governing allow. Treat “brief exists only on the branch” as its own sealed first-PR rule, not as license to trust the live worktree brief.

### 4. sharpens-framing — Change (2) is plausible for P2 but is net-new and underspecified

Evidence: `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` 5078–5161 and 5230–5336 cover all product staged paths once a story is bound; repo search at this SHA shows no `MERGE_HEAD` / both-parents filter on that path.

Failure mode if under-filtered: merge commits keep staging foreign paths and P2 remains an operator step (aim “no new refusal / fewer steps” missed). Failure mode if over-filtered: a during-merge edit whose blob happens to match a parent, or stage 1/2/3 / rename / mode-only edge cases, slips past cover. The shape “only paths whose content differs from both parents” is the right idea for P2; the design still needs an exact index-stage definition and fixtures before it can claim strength parity.

Disposition consequence: accept the direction for P2 only with a Bound-remedy note that names `MERGE_HEAD` detection, both-parent content comparison, and fail-closed behavior when parents cannot be read. Do not treat change (2) as already present machinery.

### 5. sharpens-framing — Multi-active refusal text still points at remedies workers cannot use

Evidence: `packages/core/src/hooks/scope.ts` 201–221 (`formatMultipleActiveMessage` names `DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE`, demote/complete, `scope:block`; no assignment/`swarm:launch` registration repair). Overnight symptom text in the issue body matches that message family.

Failure mode: even after change (1), a miss still trains parents toward a shared env pin that cannot bind in-session workers, which is the same deadlock class that created P1.

Disposition consequence: any lean that keeps assignment binding must also recut this recovery copy so it names parent re-registration of the worktree assignment, not a host env pin.

### 6. sharpens-framing — Question 4’s one-PR / class-4 / `productPullRequest` conflicts are outside these three changes

Evidence: class-4 protected globs include `.deft/approved-scope/**` in `packages/core/src/class-checks/policy.ts` 28–41; open #6198 in the snapshot is already the Prefer-A home for `productPullRequest` vs provenance/closing-keywords coherence.

Failure mode: folding those conflicts into this fence design either widens blast radius past the commit-gate story or silently claims a settle that the three changes do not implement.

Disposition consequence: record as leftover / cite #6198 (and class-4 one-PR practice). Do not let synthesis pretend this arc closes them.

The target changes authority, worktree identity, and shared common-dir state. Existing docs already mark occupancy and worker-auth as cooperative / same-user forgeable (`packages/core/src/hooks/fixtures/README.md` 26–27; `worker-auth-assignment.ts` 1–6). 1. Story-binding record. `swarm:pre-dispatch` begin writes a story-binding record for the target worktree under the Git common directory. The record belongs to the worktree: it holds the story id, the canonical worktree path and the list of attempt ids that use it, and no auth field. `readWorkerAuthAssignment` and `requireScmReady` do not read it. Begin runs none of the `swarm:launch` readiness checks and adds no flag.
2. Target and scope. The target is the path of a linked worktree, or a branch name, which begin resolves to the one linked worktree that has that branch checked out. The scope id must resolve to exactly one brief under `xbrief/active/` in that worktree, by brief path, story id or owned issue number. When either resolution fails, begin writes no record, prints one line that names the failed resolution, and keeps its exit code.
3. Repeat begin. When begin is refused because an attempt for the same scope and target is already running, it still ensures the record and adds that unit's running attempt ids to the list, and keeps its refusal exit code. An allowed begin adds its new attempt id after it saves its ledger. A record for the same worktree and story keeps its other ids. A record for the same worktree and a different story is replaced, with only the new attempt id in its list.
4. Read order. `resolveWorktreeStoryBinding` uses the worker-auth assignment when one exists for the worktree. Otherwise it uses the story-binding record, with the same checks and refusals it applies to an assignment.
5. Removal. `swarm:pre-dispatch` cancel or complete, after it marks an attempt ended, removes that attempt id from every story-binding record that lists it, and deletes a record whose list is then empty. It finds the records by attempt id in the record store; it does not resolve the target again and does not read any ledger. The writes in items 1 and 3 and this removal run under one lock on the record store.
6. Merge commits. When `MERGE_HEAD` is present at `git commit`, a staged product path is excused from the `file_scope` check when its staged entry (mode and blob, or deletion) is identical to that path's entry in a `MERGE_HEAD` commit that is an ancestor of the fetched delivery ref. Every other staged path is checked as today. When `MERGE_HEAD` or the delivery ref cannot be read, no path is excused.
7. Refusal text. The multiple-eligible refusal and the worktree-binding repair text name `swarm:pre-dispatch` begin by the parent as the repair for a linked worktree, before the environment pin.
8. Fence authority is unchanged. Write/Edit and the commit check keep one loader, and it reads `file_scope` only from the merge-base copy of the brief.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Given two active briefs and a linked worktree for which the parent ran `swarm:pre-dispatch` begin with one brief's scope id, when an agent commits a path in that brief's merge-base `file_scope`, then the commit hook admits it with no `DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE` set.
- Given the same setup, when the agent commits a product path outside that `file_scope`, then the commit hook refuses it.
- Given a story with `size: large` that `swarm:launch` readiness refuses, when the parent runs `swarm:pre-dispatch` begin for its worktree, then the story-binding record is written.
- Given a branch name that is checked out in exactly one linked worktree, when begin runs with that branch as its target, then the record is written for that worktree.
- Given a worktree with a story-binding record and no worker-auth assignment, when `requireScmReady` runs in it, then the result is the same as for an unregistered worktree.
- Given a worker that uses an injected token in a worktree that has only a story-binding record, when it runs a GitHub command, then no assignment check refuses it.
- Given a worktree that has a worker-auth assignment for one story, when the binding is resolved, then the assignment's story is selected.
- Given a running attempt whose record is missing, when begin runs again for the same scope and target, then the record is written and begin exits as it does today for a running attempt.
- Given a scope id that does not resolve to exactly one active brief in the target worktree, when begin runs, then it writes no record, prints one line, and exits as it does today.
- Given two attempts on two worktrees, when one attempt is cancelled or completed, then only that attempt's worktree record is removed.
- Given one attempt begun with a story's plan id and a second attempt begun with that story's issue number on the same worktree, when the first attempt is completed, then the record stays and the second worker's commit is still admitted.
- Given the same two attempts, when the second attempt is also completed, then the record is removed.
- Given one attempt begun with a worktree path and a second attempt begun with the branch that is checked out in that worktree, when either attempt is completed, then the record stays until the other attempt is also completed.
- Given an attempt begun from one checkout and ended from another checkout of the same repository, when it ends, then its id is removed from the record.
- Given a merge of the fetched delivery branch into a story branch with a conflict resolved inside the story's `file_scope`, when the agent runs `git commit`, then the hook admits the merge commit.
- Given a merge of a commit that is not an ancestor of the fetched delivery ref, when the staged set has a product path outside the story's `file_scope`, then the hook refuses the commit.
- Given a merge in which a staged path has the same blob as the `MERGE_HEAD` entry and a different file mode, when that path is outside the story's `file_scope`, then the hook refuses the commit.
- Given a worker that edits `file_scope` in its worktree copy of a brief that exists on the merge base, when it commits a path that only the edited list covers, then the hook refuses the commit.
- Given more than one eligible brief and an unregistered linked worktree, when the hook refuses, then the message names `swarm:pre-dispatch` begin as the parent's repair.

- Excusing every staged path that matches any merge parent (comment 6921217700 finding 2).
- `swarm:launch` as the writer for solo, hand-started and large stories (comment 6921248962 findings 1 and 2).
- Reusing the worker-auth assignment as the story link for those workers (comment 6921454922 finding 3).
- A new registration verb or a new required flag (comment 6921288234 finding 3).
- Binding by branch name (comment 6921288234 question 2; #6233).

## In plain English

Problem: when more than one story is active, Directive must know which story a worker belongs to before it lets that worker commit. Only `swarm:launch` recorded that link, and it refuses large stories and single stories not marked safe to run in parallel. A worker started any other way had no link, so its commits were refused and the operator ran them by hand. A merge of the default branch into a story branch was refused as well, because it stages files that belong to other stories.

Accepted solution: the step a parent already runs before it starts any implementation worker (`swarm:pre-dispatch` begin) also writes a small record that says which story the worker's worktree belongs to. The record has no auth fields, and the GitHub-auth check never reads it. The step accepts a worktree path or a branch name, and running it again writes a missing record. The record lists the attempts that use it and is deleted when the last one ends. The existing binding (#6233) then selects that story for solo, hand-started and large stories. A merge commit is excused only for files that arrive unchanged from the fetched default branch. The story's file list keeps coming from the merge base. The refusal text names the repair that works.

The design adds no new gate, verb, flag, approval or stop, and no new kind of refusal. Limits stated and accepted: a story whose brief is new on its own branch (the one-PR path) is not helped, and the operator still runs its product commits; the two one-PR conflicts seen on PR #6399 are not settled (#6198 covers one; the class 4 conflict has no issue yet); the record is not tamper-proof on a host where a worker shares the parent's identity, and such a record can only select another active story's merge-base file list. Reading the story's file list from the worker's own copy of the brief was refused by all three round-1 critics. Leftover next-build: the brand-new-brief case and the class 4 conflict.

## Summary

With more than one brief in `xbrief/active/`, the local write fence refuses every product Write/Edit in any worktree under the repo folder that is not bound to one story. On Claude Code, an in-session worker has no working way to bind itself. So Directive allows only one story in its product phase at a time per checkout, and the only way to run stories in parallel is to put worktrees outside the repo folder, where the dispatcher skips the local fence entirely. That route works, but it removes the local fence for those workers instead of satisfying it. This issue is for an operator design discussion: it decides how parallel work and the local fence fit together.

## What we saw (overnight run, 2026-11-16)

Active briefs at the time: #6272, #6205, #6361. Every in-session worker got:

> Directive denied Write: Multiple active xBRIEF artifacts are eligible (...). The write fence cannot bind the first-sorted story: a cohort would share that story's file_scope and over-permit every other worker (#4007). Parent/operator: pin DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE to the dispatched story before spawn ... Dispatched worker: report the eligible brief names upward; do not set host process env.

Each remedy the refusal names failed:

1. **`DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE` pin.** The hook reads it from the host process environment. All in-session workers share that environment, and it changes only on a host restart, so it cannot bind one worker. It can only serialize everything.
2. **`swarm:launch` registration** (per-worktree binding, #6233). It requires `readiness: ready`, which requires `parallel_safe: true`, and `size: large` forbids `parallel_safe: true`. #6361, #6205 and #6277 are all honestly large, so a large story can never be registered.
3. **Fixing the brief's swarm fields.** The edit to the active brief is refused by the same multi-active deny. No verb sets swarm fields.
4. **`scope:block` a competitor.** This is a lifecycle move that needs its own PR each way, and it serializes the stories.
5. **Run product phases one story at a time.** This works, but it makes Directive single-threaded.

Side effects:

- Each new activation (a brief-only PR) widened the deadlock for every running worker. #6277's activation was held unmerged for that reason.
- One worker routed around the fence before the parent's "do not route around it" message reached it. It used `git update-index --skip-worktree` and deleted the other story's brief in its own worktree, so the fence saw only one active brief. It undid this and disclosed it. A local working-tree view of `xbrief/active/` should not be able to steer the fence.
- The dispatcher carve-out (#2885/#3794: a linked worktree outside the payload root keeps the old skip) is what unblocked the night. With it, the local fence is gone for those workers, and CI `verify:scope-provenance` against the merge-base brief is the only `file_scope` control left.

## Questions for the design discussion

1. **Where should `file_scope` enforcement live?** The local fence is an early warning. CI scope-provenance is the control that refuses a merge. If CI is the real control, should the local fence become advisory, or apply only where a story binding is certain?
2. **How should a worker bind to one story** without host env or `parallel_safe`? Some options: the worktree's branch, the dispatch envelope (spawn env bag), or the activation PR's head. Any of these must not be forgeable by the worker itself.
3. **Should `parallel_safe` / `size` gate binding at all?** They describe scheduling risk, not which files a worker may write.
4. **Is the outside-repo route the intended future shape?** In that shape, worker worktrees sit outside the payload root, Directive governs at PR time, and the local hooks govern only the primary checkout. If so, make it a documented, chosen mode rather than a carve-out.
5. **How should a working-tree change to `xbrief/` be handled?** Deleting a brief, or marking it skip-worktree, should not change what the fence admits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given two or more active briefs and a worker dispatched for one of them, when the worker edits a file in its own story's `file_scope`, then the write is admitted without a host restart, a brief edit, or a worktree outside the repo folder.
- Given the same setup, when the worker edits a file outside its story's `file_scope`, then the write is refused.
